author: Escanor89
quote:
The Good Guy Simp Simulator, A $2 Billion Social Experiment

A 5.5 user score? Honestly, I'm not surprised. This whole project feels less like a video game and more like a social experiment in modern entertainment, corporate messaging and manufactured controversy. 13 years in development, a reported budget of up to $2 billion, endless marketing hype and awards-season attention before players even had the chance to properly experience the finished product. 

And somehow we're supposed to believe this represents the pinnacle of gaming?To me, the writing and character portrayal feel increasingly artificial. Male characters come across as deliberately weakened caricatures, while supposedly progressive messaging often feels forced rather than organically integrated into the story. It's almost like the Good Guy Simp Simulator: an endless parade of manufactured outrage, predictable character dynamics and ideological signalling instead of genuinely compelling storytelling.

And here's the bigger question: Why are developers so increasingly disconnected from what a substantial part of their audience actually wants? Why does so much modern entertainment seem more interested in provoking, dividing and lecturing its audience than simply telling a great story?I'm not interested in turning this into a political debate about men versus women, left versus right, or any particular culture. I just want good writing, interesting characters, creative freedom and games that respect their audience. The gaming industry increasingly feels like a corporate circus built around hype, brand management and consumer manipulation. 

The physical media situation at Sony was another wake-up call for me.I eventually sold my PS5, and honestly, I don't miss it.I'm discovering new hobbies, spending more time outdoors, enjoying family life and investing my money in experiences that actually add something meaningful to my life. Gaming used to be about escapism, creativity and genuine fun. Maybe it's time we stopped treating billion-dollar corporations like they're doing us a favour.

My money, my time, my choice. And Boys who learned It the hard way: I hope you all get your refunds <3

author: Escanor89
quote: I was able to meet the German developers from North Rhine-Westphalia in person at Gamescom in Cologne in 2023. As someone who works at a university hospital and sees terrible things every day and feels completely powerless, this game left me emotionally and emphatically charged and shaken up. In these few hours, you can see in a nutshell what the German hospital system is like. Lack of funds, power-hungry individuals who act as if the patients are important when only the turnover is important. Doctors who at first seem very grim and bitter, but who have been working in this system for so long to help people and see no way out except to carry on or change professions..Apart from a few bugs, some of which are more funny than annoying, this is a very good game IF you don't compare it with other similar games. In the early stages, I often compared the game to Night in the Woods. Although both games pursue completely different interests and stories. So I gave the game another chance a year later and I'm glad I did. It's true, it's difficult to get into the game, to get interested in “most” of the characters. The only ones I really cared about were the old turtle lady, Mia, Karl and the doctor on our ward.Nevertheless, I really enjoyed the game with its 6-10 hours of playtime and often had to think about how and whether it could go on like this. Similar to the aforementioned Night in the Woods, after playing the game you feel like a grain of sand in the universe and question your decisions in **** my opinion a very deep game for a team that has developed their FIRST GAME. Congratulations to my fellow countrymen.

author: Escanor89
quote:
This game has been out for far too long and I've missed it for far too long for what it's trying to tell.

My wife and I played Night in the Woods for Christmas 2022, I knew it was a story game but didn't expect anything.

What I got back was a reflection of my life, my dreams, I was able to reflect on the lives of others and how difficult they have it at times and I trample on my happiness.

I cried several times in the game, felt caught up, felt like I was back in my school days and had an insane amount of friends that grew on me and most importantly, I learned a lot about myself and my career and that no matter what you do, the most important thing is that you get together with the right people.

Night in the Woods has an incredible storytelling that is both playful and serious.

The only thing that disturbed me in between, attention small spoiler! was the dreams where you had to constantly run back and forth which felt to me like you were just trying to stretch out the game time.

I will play through the game countless times and make it my October game, come what may every October in the year this game is unpacked again, cried, rejoiced and reflected again on their own lives!
